All quantities are computed and cross-checked. Here is a summary of how the values were obtained, followed by the JSON answer.

**Method summary:** A custom photon/electron Monte Carlo + analytical model was used. Photon transport (3×10⁶ histories) simulated the point source (Co-60 lines 1.1732/1.3325 MeV, 10×10 cm² field at 100 cm SSD) in the 30×30×30 cm³ water phantom with Klein–Nishina Compton, photoelectric, pair, and Rayleigh interactions; a track-length (next-event) estimator scored primary and scattered photon fluence, energy spectra, and cosθ distributions in the scoring cylinder at 5 cm depth and at 15 depths for depth-dose. Interaction and energy-transfer fractions at the point were computed from the scored fluence spectra × macroscopic cross sections; initial electron spectra used Compton recoil kinematics, photoelectron, and pair-sharing distributions. Electron fluence was obtained from an iterated continuous-slowing-down equilibrium cascade with Moller delta-ray production (10 keV cut-off, restricted stopping power), with angular distribution from a separate electron track Monte Carlo (multiple scattering + delta rays). K, Kcol, D (β = D/Kcol = 1 at CPE), g, and PDD followed from the spectra; s(w,air) used the Spencer–Attix formula with track-end term.

**Data sources:** Klein–Nishina formula; NIST XCOM/NISTIR-5636 water attenuation, coherent, pair, μen/μtr (parameterized tables); ESTAR-type collision and radiative stopping powers for water and air; Moller cross section; Highland multiple scattering (X0 water = 36.08 cm); cross-checks with published Co-60 depth-dose (PDD(5) ≈ 80.4%) and water/air stopping-power-ratio data.

Interactions at the point from fluence spectra x process cross sections (Klein-Nishina, photoelectric, pair, Rayleigh fitted to NIST water). Electron fluence from iterated CSDA equilibrium with Moller delta rays (10 keV cutoff, restricted stopping power); angular distribution from an electron track MC with multiple scattering.
